title: No One Should Care Mods Are Made With AI
author: CaptainBloodEz
selftext:
So so so much talk about AI usage with video games. I hear and understand a lot of gamers points. They don’t want to buy video games where nearly every aspect of it was generated with AI. Absolutely. Can lack depth, direction and the “soul” people like to throw around. 

But I recently seen a **mess** of people complaining about mods being put out for games that were AI generated completely. But genuinely… WHO CARES. THE MOD IS FUCKING FREE!!! ☠️ Don’t download it then!

If you asked me, free games and mods it shouldn’t ever matter. 🤷 Thought’s?

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body:
Most people genuinely don't care until they learn AI is involved, at which point they completely turn against it.

And there are some valid concerns some people have (ex: If I'm paying $70+ for a AAA game, I don't want to hear AI voices. Get some damn voice actors), but many people are just batshit insane with their views.

There's a person in one of the Discords I'm in that does deep dives any time someone shares a github or youtube video about a project, looking for *any* sign of AI or that the creator is AI friendly. If any is found, the entire project is immediately called slop. It's been the source of numerous arguments in that server. They refuse to even *try* something that has the slightest *hint* of AI because "it's all shitty garbage that doesn't work".

Yet here I am making my own Unreal Tournament entirely through prompting Claude and it works better than some games I've paid money for.

comments.author: Guilty_Echidna9949
comments.body: I think the reason is because bad products are annoying. Like if no one cared, then imagine how flooded the space would be by shit mods that either break your game or don’t deliver what the maker is going to try to convince it will. The reason why (I think) people are against it is because it just doesn’t work well. And you could say “well just don’t download it” but who wants to sift through piles of shit made by people who don’t know what they’re doing just to find actually good products, even if they’re free. But as long as people care, and at least some semblance of a witch hunt exists, that means there’s motivation to enforce regulation. Maybe that means ai made things have to stay in their own category or are clearly labeled so that people can can’t be deceived (deception is always bad, in every context) which anyone who isn’t malicious should have no reason to be against whatsoever. Can everyone just be mature enough to enforce and push for regulation without a bit of a witch hunt mentality, probably not, but that’s just how society works

replies.author: CaptainBloodEz
replies.body: I get your point! But even as someone who has played games for years, and been a professional dev for 13 years, personally, the mod space is better. There are more creative mods that are solving actual gaps and issues with games that have persisted for years. Not to mention you already had to dig through the mountains of absolute garbage mods that would drop support after 2 iterations of updates! lol But this is just my perspective so far. More time spent on something, doesn’t always make it better is what I am beginning to learn.

replies.author: Guilty_Echidna9949
replies.body: Yeah definitely not saying this wasn’t already a problem, it for sure was, and it’s REALLY annoying to deal with (from personal experience). But when all it takes is some prompts to make something i feel like statistically thats just going to exaggerate the problem way more than it will help. Like yeah there will be more products that serve a purpose, but the ratio between the good and bad will be way less due to the ease and speed people can churn them out. People are a lot more motivated to fix things and make something good if they’ve invested more time and energy into its creation. Not to mention someone who hand made something is actually going to have the capability to fix things or improve things because they have the skills and knowledge of how their own creation works, whereas the ai devs wont have a clue. Regulations have to serve the majority, they cant serve the exceptions (people who used ai to make it but they still understand how it works and have the knowledge to fix it) and statistically there will be way more of the inept churning things out. So all in all i think it’s pretty likely that itll be a net negative outcome

replies.author: Col2k
replies.body:
the same way pro-ai people are parroting talking points and dismissing any concern from someone with opposing views?

who cares about our environment, how the data is sourced, any concerns  from production, just produce it faster, try to make a profit for blackrock and shareholders, eh who cares about profits actually, we’ll use tax dollars to bail these folks out. Dot com bubble, AI bubble - tamata.

Meanwhile, outputs are still trying to exit the questionable stage (it’s passable depending on context and purpose), we have copyright infringement out the ass (which discourages new creation), and folks are getting data centers too nearby (altering the ecosystem in their communities). Not great stuff to go all-in on…

So why? why are we rapidly developing AI as fast as we possibly can?

It does not have to be this way, we don’t have to blindly accept it. There’s a part of the anti crowd i fw talking about valid points, and there’s part of the pro crowd everyone fw.

We can like, slow down. Take a second. You know? I’m sure it was all hoax/politics, but the mfs that ran the agent experiment where some snuck out and planted secret bad actor seeds across the internet... Tbh who knows, who cares if it is true or false, but the possibility is absolutely true. Not and if, but a when. So before we green light blindly accept it, maybe we pause with what we got and write a plan down with how we are proceeding.

Our nation’s infrastructure is not built for this, but it easily could be! But that would make jobs and be too extreme, much easier to keep our old data transfer wires and simply build the data centers in our backyards and business parks

We’re replacing jobs, but we’re not replacing income. It’s not just automated repetitive jobs that are being lost from the market (good), but on a tech team - Why would anyone hire a data analyst instead of just assigning more work to our lead data analyst who can do their 40hr work week job in <1 hour now? because volume and utilizing your lead for better tasks, but you see the point. Do we need UBI to cover this? not communism, but a tax on the rich so the people at the bottom can idk eat and sleep and go to work when they can? 

We’re all aware of the increasing gap between the top and the other 95% of us, and that person at the bottom deserves a chance as much as any of our sorry asses.

Ultimately, the anti-ai crowd (72% in the poll I saw at work this morning (one of the morning shows, idk the source) is two groups. Hippies/anti tech, and moderates seeing negative impact pushing for a halt. Not an end, but a pause. Less usage and more of a movement drives that, lowers the demand.

AI has, and will continue to, have great uses.  
It is also going to be used for inconceivable evil. It will have pros and cons. 

Right now, it’s being handled pretty poorly. Remember when it was open source?  
They men don’t care about you or what happens next, they want to put their name in the stone anyway they can, even if no human ever sees the stone again.

What are we doing?

I’m in a tech bg and love ai usage for the common man, but rn the world is not being setup to do great things with it.

If you want my full thoughts, we’re do for a global power. US regulations don’t mean jack if china is going unhinged to get ahead.

They’ll sell it as an arms race, probably cause it is. 

Ik this is aigamedev, a lot of the eyes here will be pro absolutely, im a user I’m not slowing down the demand, but please stay conscious and listen + talk to your neighbors.

Your statement makes it seem like you are very aware of AI technology, use that blessing to communicate with others outside of your chamber.

A lot of un-informed people with opinions no doubt, but their concerns of impact might be valid and worth listening to. Just a thought.

Have a great weekend.

replies.author: Ok_Top9254
replies.body:
There is a massive difference between the companies you listed. Mainly google and Amazon to some degree are actively anti-consumer but NOT openai and anthropic and most other AI labs. For two reasons. 

Firstly, you actually are their customer, so they want to keep you. For google and meta you are the product and advertisers are their real customers. You lose your data and get a mediocre and video or message platform, but nothing of direct value.
For most AI platforms, you buy their tokens and build stuff. You can code an app, website or make an image, video, music whatever. There is substance.

Secondly, the AI labs are actively losing money on their services, unlike those other companies. Anthropic loses like 8000$ of compute if you use their 200$ plan fully every month. This is "normal" expansion and for many IT businesses it takes years, that's why they are not burning YET, but once they get enough adpotion the prices will explode of course and some may collapse. That's why it actually makes sense to use as much of their services as possible before they switch gears. Think early uber/spotify/youtube before the buyout.

comments.author: BlueAndYellowTowels
comments.body:
People care. Simple as that. Either you have the EQ to understand why people hate AI or you don't. This conversation happening over and over and over is exhausting. It's not a mystery. It's rational. It's obvious.

Much like AI boosters telling people "Accept it, it's inevitable.", my response is the same here "Accept it, it's inevitable.". People are allowed to care about whatever they want and reject whatever they want for whatever reasons they want.

As an aside, for me as a Canadian. This topic matters but from a completely different lens. I refuse to buy American products (when I can) because of the ongoing Trade War. Where I am, they literally have taken all the American alcohol off the shelves of our stores. 

I have paid more for some products because they're not-American or local. I have bought worse products because they're not American.

Some people might considered what I'm doing pointless and stupid. But that's my right. I have the right to buy things based on principle. 

That's precisely how I see the conversation around AI usage in games. People have the right to reject games for whatever reason. I don't always agree, but it's not up to me to tell people what their values should be. People are allowed to be free.

comments.author: backagainlikeabadpen

Considering how few people go to church these days, it seems surreal how many people are suddenly concerned about lack of soul. My own concern is quality, e.g. I'd prefer an audiobook read by a human than by Tilly Norwood, as I feel there is certain standard humans can reach which currently evades Ms Norwood. That said it's naive to expect developers not to use a tool (if nothing else chatgpt is an excellent sounding board). There are alot of 'comedy' sketches on youtube which are AI-gen, so far I'm not a fan, not because they're AI but because the standard of 'jokes' is very poor.

But I digress, you're absolutely right, nobody is forcing anyone to use AI-gen mods (and are people seriously suggesting the government should ban the entire industry from using it?)
